realism_constraints: No modern forensic technology such as DNA or advanced ballistics
Limited communication means, telegraph and letters primary
Social and legal norms emphasize family honor and discretion
location: Q 2 Ranch, Quilter County, eastern Oregon
institution: County coroner's inquest and local law enforcement
crime_subtype: planned assisted death disguised as murder

cast.name: Neal Quilter
cast.motive_seed: fear of disgrace, complex about marriage
cast.alibi_window: locked in room at time of murder

surface_summary: Richard Quilter was found shot in his locked room with no footprints outside and a rope hanging from the window, suggesting an impossible escape. Family members were locked in their rooms, and suspicion fell on Neal Quilter, who confessed but had an alibi. The case appears to be a locked-room murder with a mysterious masked intruder.
accepted_facts: Richard Quilter was shot in his bed on October 8, 1900
All family members except Irene were locked in their rooms at the time
No footprints were found outside the house after the murder
A rope was found hanging from the victim's window, covered with snow
inferred_conclusions: Neal Quilter was the murderer despite his locked-room alibi
The murderer escaped using the rope from the window
Olympe Quilter was involved in the murder due to her eccentric behavior
mechanism_description: Richard Quilter, terminally ill with cancer, planned his own death to appear as murder to secure insurance money for his family. Dr. Joseph Elm, the family doctor, assisted by killing Richard at his request to spare him suffering and protect the family's future. Neal Quilter's apparent guilt was due to his amnesia and confusion, not actual involvement.
delivery_path: Richard Quilter arranged for his death to look like murder
Dr. Joseph Elm agreed to assist and planned the act
Richard was shot in his bed by Dr. Elm
The rope and locked doors were staged to mislead investigators
Neal Quilter, suffering amnesia, believed he was the murderer
Family members were locked in rooms to create alibis
Dr. Elm concealed the true cause and circumstances until confession
outcome_result: Dr. Joseph Elm confesses to assisting Richard Quilter's planned death, exonerating Neal and the family.

false_assumption.statement: The murderer escaped the house using the rope hanging from the window.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The presence of the rope dangling from the window and the absence of footprints outside suggest an escape route. The locked doors and no footprints imply the killer must have used the rope.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The rope was a staged clue by the victim and doctor to mislead investigators; the killer never escaped that way.

supporting_points: Neal confessed to the murder in letters
He was found locked in his room after the shot
Family members believed he was guilty due to his behavior
He had motive related to family tensions and inheritance
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Neal's locked-room alibi and the timing of the shot make it physically impossible for him to have committed the murder

red_herrings.description: Olympe's theory that Archie Biggil, Irene's ex-husband, came masked and committed the murder
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Archie was locked in a trunk and never searched; the story was a fabrication

red_herrings.description: Olympe's fainting and the discharged .32 Colt's revolver suggested she might have accidentally shot Richard
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The revolver was unloaded and the shot was from a .38 caliber gun; Olympe's story was a staged distraction

closed_circle.rationale: All were present in the house at the time, with locked doors and no footprints outside, making the suspect pool limited to family members and close associates.

authority_sources: district attorney's office representative Benjamin Thopson

inference_path.observation: No footprints found outside the house after the murder
inference_path.correction: The murderer did not escape through the window using the rope
inference_path.effect: The killer must have remained inside the house
required_evidence: Inspection of snow-covered porch roof showing no footprints
Testimony of family members about locked doors and keys

inference_path.observation: Neal Quilter confessed to the murder in letters
inference_path.correction: Neal was locked in his room and had amnesia about the event
inference_path.effect: Neal's confession is unreliable and he is innocent
required_evidence: Lucy Quilter's testimony about finding Neal locked in his room
Neal's letters and mental health evaluations

inference_path.observation: Olympe Quilter fainted and had an unloaded .32 Colt's revolver
inference_path.correction: The murder weapon was a .38 Colt's, different caliber
inference_path.effect: Olympe could not have fired the fatal shot
required_evidence: Discovery of unloaded .32 Colt's revolver under Olympe's pillow

inference_path.observation: Insurance company claims death was suicide to deny payout
inference_path.correction: Death was planned assisted death to appear as murder
inference_path.effect: Motive for murder is invalid; death was mercy killing
required_evidence: Insurance policy payment records and inquest testimony

inference_path.observation: Dr. Joseph Elm claimed to be in Portland at time of murder
inference_path.correction: Dr. Elm secretly assisted in killing Richard Quilter
inference_path.effect: Dr. Elm is the true culprit acting on victim's request
required_evidence: Dr. Elm's confession to Lynn MacDonald
Discrepancies in alibi and medical knowledge of victim's condition

inference_path.observation: Red mask mentioned as victim's dying words
inference_path.correction: Red mask was a staged clue by Olympe to mislead investigators
inference_path.effect: The red mask is a false clue, not evidence of an intruder
required_evidence: Discovery of red satin mask in Olympe's room

inference_path.observation: Family members were locked in their rooms with keys collected
inference_path.correction: Victim and Dr. Elm planned the locking to create alibis
inference_path.effect: Locked rooms do not exclude family members from involvement
required_evidence: Testimony about keys found on bedside tables
Letters describing the locking of doors and family movements

discriminating_test.design: Reenact the night of the murder with all family members locked in their rooms and keys collected as described. Attempt to replicate Neal's alleged movement from his locked room to the victim's room and back within the time window. Also, test the possibility of the rope being used for escape by physically assessing the porch roof and window access under similar conditions.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The reenactment will show that Neal could not have left his locked room and returned in the short time available, and that the rope could not have been used for escape due to snow coverage and physical difficulty.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: If Neal cannot physically perform the movements required within the time constraints and no footprints appear on the roof or ground, the theory of Neal's guilt and rope escape is disproven.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with detailed letters, testimonies, and descriptions of the locked rooms, the rope, and the absence of footprints. The distinction between the .32 and .38 caliber guns is clearly stated. The victim's terminal illness and the insurance policy details are disclosed. The psychological state and amnesia of Neal are explored, allowing attentive readers to question his guilt. The final confession and explanation by Dr. Elm are foreshadowed by clues in the letters and testimonies, making the solution accessible.

anchors.claim: The victim was shot in bed with a .38 caliber bullet
anchors.anchor: Death was caused by an intrathoracic hemorrhage, due to a bullet shot into the left chest

anchors.claim: No footprints were found outside the house after the murder
anchors.anchor: Nowhere near a window, nowhere near a door, was there a footprint nor a break in the snow

anchors.claim: Family members were locked in their rooms with keys collected
anchors.anchor: Irene found seven keys in my brother’s room, and used one key to unlock each door

anchors.claim: Neal Quilter was locked in his room at the time of the murder
anchors.anchor: Lucy came running into my room in her nightgown, screaming my name

anchors.claim: The rope hanging from the window was covered with snow and unused
anchors.anchor: The rope was covered with snow, and there was not a handprint in the snow on the window sill

anchors.claim: Olympe’s revolver was a .32 Colt’s and was unloaded
anchors.anchor: It was Uncle Phineas’s old .32 Colt’s. I broke it. The chambers were all empty

anchors.claim: The murder weapon was a .38 caliber Colt’s
anchors.anchor: The bullet, which Dr. Joe had removed from Father’s body, had been fired from a .38 Colt’s of fairly recent make

anchors.claim: Dr. Joseph Elm confessed to assisting in the murder
anchors.anchor: I killed Dick. That’s a damn lie! And you know it! Take it easy, boy, if you can. I’m sorry

anchors.claim: The victim was terminally ill with cancer
anchors.anchor: Your father’s ailment was cancer. He knew it, and I knew it

anchors.claim: The victim planned his own death to look like murder
anchors.anchor: Dick planned alone, and we planned together. By Gad, Neal, but we tried

anchors.claim: The victim’s last words mentioned a red mask
anchors.anchor: He said, quite distinctly, “Red mask.” There was no shaking her certainty about that

anchors.claim: The red mask was found in Olympe’s room
anchors.anchor: Lying on the floor, directly beneath the open cupola window, was a mask, large enough to cover a man’s entire face, cut roughly out of bright red satin

anchors.claim: Neal Quilter suffered amnesia about the murder
anchors.anchor: I am swearing to you that, for the past two years or more, until about half an hour ago, I have thought exactly the same thing about myself

anchors.claim: Neal Quilter’s letters contain clues to the truth
anchors.anchor: Lucy’s second letter to you makes the first track. Maybe it would take a crime analyst to discover it

anchors.claim: The family’s insurance policy had lapsed but was paid by Dr. Elm
anchors.anchor: I made that last payment, he said, and sat down

anchors.claim: The family dog Whatof was chained at the front door
anchors.anchor: We have kept Whatof chained by the front door and Keeper chained by the back door

anchors.claim: The inquest jury returned a verdict of death by person unknown
anchors.anchor: Died on the night of October eighth, from the results of a gunshot wound inflicted by person or persons unknown

anchors.claim: The victim’s bed was moved slightly
anchors.anchor: The bed had been moved three or four inches at the foot—pulled along over the carpet

anchors.claim: Irene Quilter was locked out of her room and slept on the sofa
anchors.anchor: She found that the door was locked. She turned around and sneaked straight downstairs again, and fixed herself a bed, with Indian blankets, on the sofa

anchors.claim: The victim’s window was open with a rope tied to the bed
anchors.anchor: The window was wide open from the bottom. There was a thick rope hanging over the sill and out of it
